newsitem.title: CHINA: China copper supply greater than demand- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China copper supply greater than demand- newspaper.

text.p: China's copper supplies are currently greater than demand and copper prices are unlikely to rise significantly in the short term, the China Securities newspaper said on Saturday.
In January and February, domestic output and imports of copper amounted to 165,000 tonnes, an increase of 18.5 percent against the same period last year, the newspaper said.
Of this, domestic output was 146,000 tonnes, a rise of 11.9 percent and imports were 19,000 tonnes, a rise of 30.2 percent, it said.
Demand in the two months was estimated to have increased by 14 percent against the same period of last year, a much lower growth rate than supply, it said.

By the end of February, China's copper prices were at an average of 21,000 yuan per tonne, an increase of 3.9 percent against the start of this year but a drop of 18.3 percent against the same period last year, the newspaper said.
"Although copper prices in some cities have regained some ground this year, the overall market has not emerged from the shadow of the price slump last year," it said.
